title: The starter Button Primary shines like the mock and its Icon field shows the icon
goal: The Library Button now comes in the mock's nine looks, but its Primary look is a flat blue where the variants mock draws a soft gloss, and the Icon field on a copy shows only the word where the mock shows the icon in front of it. Bring both up to the mock so the first button somebody drops looks finished.
notes: From the-starter-button-comes-as-primary-secondary-or (2026-10-09). Starter looks: Sources/PhotonzCore/StarterComponents.swift button(pen,variant,size), paints from named styles (StarterStyle), so a gradient means either a gradient Paint on the Background fill bound to Accent (Paint supports gradients, check ColorStyleBinding with a gradient) or a highlight layer. Icon face: Sources/Photonz/ComponentPanel.swift choiceMenu/choiceKnob passes no glyph to VideoKit.Dropdown; SelectFace has swatch and showsComponentMark only, so it needs a leading image. Menu rows already carry template pictures (choicePicture). Mock: docs/design/mocks/pages/ui-variants.html .pmatrix and #iconTrigger; docs/design/mocks/shared/components/button.css .btn.primary/.btn.secondary.
acceptance: The Primary look of a dropped Button has the mock's soft top to bottom gradient and lighter top edge (button.css .btn.primary), and still repaints when the Accent style is recoloured
On a picked Button copy the Icon field shows the picked icon's glyph in front of its name, as ui-variants.html #iconTrigger draws it, legible in light and dark
The Secondary look reads like the mock's glass control over a coloured backdrop, or a decision card settles keeping it a plain surface
starter-button-looks-walk photographs all three at Next defaults

log.note: Adversarial pass: the mock's Primary is a white wash over the accent (accent 84%/white 16% at top to accent), a 1px white .45 inset top edge and an accent glow. Making the Background fill a gradient would break its Accent binding (reconcile compares paints), so the gloss goes on as a separate unbound white Shine piece over the accent, the top edge as an inner shadow, and the glow as a drop shadow whose colour is bound to Accent. Recolouring Accent then repaints fill and glow and the wash stays white. Secondary: no backdrop blur exists in the renderer, so glass can only be translucency (white 74%, the mock's --glass); will judge it over a coloured backdrop before deciding vs a card. Icon face: SelectFace has no leading picture; adding one fed from the same template picture the menu rows use.

Built: Primary gets an unbound white Shine piece (linear 180deg, #FFFFFF14 to clear), an inner white top edge (30%, 1pt, sharp) and an accent drop glow (6 down, 8 soft, -6 spread, 60%) whose colour is bound to Accent; Secondary Background at 74% opacity (mock --glass); Icon field face shows the picked icon as a template picture (SelectFace.leadImage), nil when Mixed or No icon. Numbers are smaller than the mock's (16%/45%) because the renderer mixes in linear light; StarterComponentRenderTests.thePrimaryButtonShinesLikeTheMock holds rendered rows to the mock's sRGB sums. New walk starter-button-shine-walk on a new dark-artboard fixture; 17 other walks that drop a Button all green; full suite 11968 tests green. Filed the-starter-secondary-button-frosts-what-is-behi (p2) for backdrop blur. Left rough, not filed: the Shine is a visible piece in the original's layer list.

Primary now has the mock's gloss (white wash piece over Accent), lighter top edge and Accent-bound glow; recolouring Accent repaints capsule and glow. Secondary is the mock's 74% glass. The Icon field shows the picked icon before its name in light and dark. Core tests (StarterButtonLooksTests, render test against the mock's colours) and the full suite (11968) green; starter-button-looks-walk and new starter-button-shine-walk photograph all three at Next defaults; 17 other Button walks green.
